$comment: PE32+ DYNAMIC-LINK LIBRARY (.dll) for x86_64 Windows -- c152, the D-LK2-4 anchor (plan 14 / roadmap A2): the PE mirror of the c150 ELF .so. Consumed by `src/link/format/pe.cpp` via the format-blind linker engine: `pe.type = dll` routes to the SAME `encodeExec` substrate the .exe image uses, with the dll divergences (IMAGE_FILE_DLL in Characteristics, AddressOfEntryPoint = 0, a `.edata` export directory wired into data-directory[0], ImageBase = the 0x180000000 MSVC DLL convention). The REAL Windows loader consumes the output: `ctypes.CDLL('dsslib.dll').dss_add(2, 40)` loads + GetProcAddress-binds + calls it. Differs from pe64-x86_64-windows-exec.format.json in: `pe.type` (dll vs exec), `pe.characteristics` 0x2022 = EXECUTABLE_IMAGE|LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE|IMAGE_FILE_DLL (dumpbin ground truth for `cl /LD`: a DLL sets BOTH 0x0002 and 0x2000 -- EXECUTABLE_IMAGE means 'valid image', not 'is a .exe'), NO `entryPoint`/`processExit`/`entryCallingConvention`/`processArgs` (a DSS DLL ships with AddressOfEntryPoint = 0 -- NO DllMain; the loader treats entry 0 as 'skip process/thread notifications', a legal PE documented in the loader's LdrpCallInitRoutine path and produced by `link /NOENTRY`; the DllMain arm is the pinned follow-up D-LK2-DLL-DLLMAIN-ENTRY -- validate() rejects the entry cluster here exactly as the ELF dyn schema rejects it on the .so shape), `optionalHeader.imageBase` 0x180000000 (MSVC .dll default; the loader rebases via `.reloc` when the preferred base is taken or ASLR slides it -- DYNAMIC_BASE stays set so the DIR64 machinery is exercised for real), `optionalHeader.subsystem` 2 (GUI -- the `cl /LD` convention; the loader ignores the subsystem for a library loaded into an existing process) and `optionalHeader.dllCharacteristics` 0x160 (HIGH_ENTROPY_VA|DYNAMIC_BASE|NX_COMPAT -- dumpbin ground truth; link.exe does NOT set TERMINAL_SERVER_AWARE on DLLs, it is a per-process flag), NO `tlsAccess` and NO tdata/tbss rows (static TLS in a LoadLibrary'd DLL is its own loader-interaction arc -- D-LK-DLL-TLS-MODEL; every thread_local fails loud at the linker's supportedDataSections gate by this set's absence), `artifactProfiles` ["lib"], and NO `librarySynthesis` (the win32 <threads.h> shim vehicle inside a DLL is an UNTESTED form -- a threads.h-using lib fails loud at the synth pass rather than shipping unwitnessed machinery; the exec sibling keeps it). The export-directory DllName field is emitted EMPTY: per-artifact identity does not belong in a shipped format schema (the same decision as the dyn sibling's absent DT_SONAME) -- GetProcAddress never reads it and DSS emits no forwarder RVAs, the only consumer of that name.
$stackReserveUnsupportedReasonComment: D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH: this .dll schema declares WHY it cannot carry a per-program stack reserve, so a `stackReserve` / `--stack-reserve` request against it is REFUSED with an actionable remedy instead of silently writing a field nothing reads. The optionalHeader below DOES carry sizeOfStackReserve/sizeOfStackCommit (1 MiB / 4 KiB) and they are INERT for a DLL: the Windows loader sizes a thread's stack from the EXECUTABLE that loads the module (its own header) or from CreateThread's explicit dwStackSize -- documented Win32 semantics (`dwStackSize` of 0 "uses the default size for the executable"), and MEASURED on this machine: 12 unrelated Microsoft system DLLs (ntdll, ucrtbase, kernel32, msvcrt, shell32, crypt32, user32, gdi32, ole32, advapi32, ws2_32, wintrust) all carry the IDENTICAL untuned 0x40000, while 8 system EXEs carry tuned VARYING values (0x80000 / 0x100000) with SizeOfStackCommit spread over 8 KiB..1008 KiB. Uniformity across unrelated DLLs vs per-program tuning on EXEs is the signature of a field nothing reads. NOTE the values here are DSS's 1 MiB convention, not MS's 0.25 MiB -- deliberately left alone: the field is inert either way, so changing it would be churn with no observable effect.
$dataModelComment: Same LLP64 identity as the exec sibling (64-bit Windows).
$headerNameMatchingComment: D-PP-HEADER-CASE-INSENSITIVE-PE: Windows filesystems (NTFS, FAT) match file names case-INSENSITIVELY, and the Windows SDK depends on it -- sqlite3.c:67322 spells `#include <Windows.h>` with a capital W while the shipped descriptor is `windows.json`. REQUIRED closed-enum field. DSS ASCII-folds the comparison ITSELF per path component (core/types/include_path_resolve.cpp) instead of asking fs::exists, so this resolves identically whether the build host is NTFS or ext4 -- MEASURED before the axis existed: rc=0 through /mnt/c, rc=1 error[F001A] on ext4, SAME binary, SAME commit.
$cSymbolDecorationComment: D-FFI-CMANGLING-RULE-NOT-CONFIG-DRIVEN: PE/COFF x64 applies NO decoration to a C identifier. The leading-underscore cdecl convention belongs to 32-bit x86 PE, which DSS does not ship; the 32-bit `_func` and stdcall `_func@N` rules arrive as their own scheme enumerators WITH their engine arms, never as a re-spelling of this one. MEASURED 2026-08-06 (`objdump -p C:/Windows/System32/ucrtbase.dll`, GNU binutils via WSL): the UCRT exports `exit`, `_exit` AND `_Exit` as three DISTINCT entries -- so the underscored spelling is not a decoration of `exit` here either, it already names a different function, and a format that wrongly claimed `leading-underscore` would silently bind to it. Consistent with this family's own `processExit.importMangledName`, the undecorated `exit`. This key is the single owner of a fact that previously had TWO: the closed C++ table `kCManglingRules` (src/ffi/mangling/c_mangle.cpp, keyed on ObjectFormatKind) and, redundantly, a literal encoding in the descriptors themselves -- the macho64-*-exec files spell `processExit.importMangledName` as `_exit` while their elf/pe siblings spell it `exit`. Two owners in two languages, with nothing forcing them to agree. RED-ON-DISABLE, stated precisely for the tier that exists today (MEASURED 2026-08-06 by actually removing the key from a shipped file and running the suite): DELETE this key and the format is REFUSED AT LOAD -- TWO errors at /cSymbolDecoration, one C_MissingField from the loader and one from ObjectFormatData::validate(), which loadFromText runs before returning -- so every test and example that loads this format goes red, naming the file. CHANGING the value is now an equally REAL lever, and this sentence was corrected the moment it became true: before step C4 the engine still read a C++ table and the value here changed no emitted binary. C4 landed (same cycle, TF-C122), and the effect is MEASURED 2026-08-06 -- flipping macho64-arm64-darwin-exec from `leading-underscore` to `none` and RECOMPILING NOTHING made the engine emit `printf` where it had emitted `_printf`, reddening tests/ffi/test_c_mangle.cpp's SchemeIsReadFromTheShippedSchemaNotACppTable. That is the whole point of the anchor: the answer lives in this file, so editing this file changes what the compiler emits. Two further pins guard the value: tests/link/test_c_symbol_decoration.cpp asserts the per-kind answer across all 24 shipped files and cross-checks it against this family's own processExit.importMangledName.
$cCallingConventionComment: D-FFI-ABI-CATALOG-SELECTS-CALLING-CONVENTION-BY-FORMAT-IDENTITY: the platform C ABI for code compiled into this format, NAMING a row in the paired target's callingConventions[] array. Microsoft x64 (`rcx,rdx,r8,r9` + 32 bytes of shadow space) — the SAME x86_64 processor as the elf64/macho64 descriptors, a DIFFERENT convention, which is why the fact is per-FORMAT and cannot live on the target.
$outputExtensionComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: the extension the driver appends to an artifact this format produces. This used to be derived in C++ by `program/target_spec.cpp::outputExtensionFor`, a five-arm `switch (fmt.kind())` with a NESTED per-flavor switch inside each arm -- seven identity mentions computing a NAMING fact, which is not an engine behaviour at all. The nest existed because one ObjectFormatKind spans several artifact flavors; a DOCUMENT is exactly one flavor, so the whole derivation collapses to this one string. REQUIRED on every format. An EMPTY value is a DECLARED answer and not an omission -- a Unix executable carries no extension -- which is why the in-memory field is an `optional` and the loader's required check asks `contains`, never `empty`.
$archiveFlavorComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: WHICH `ar` variant this format's ECOSYSTEM uses. Declared on every native format, not only the `container: archive` ones, because that is what the deleted C++ derivation answered: `(format.kind() == ObjectFormatKind::Pe) ? Coff : SysV` was handed WHATEVER format the caller had, and `linkAndWriteStaticArchive` is reachable with the RELOCATABLE format of an ecosystem as well as its archive one (MEASURED -- restricting the key to archives reddened link/test_ar_writer and program/test_static_link). NOT cosmetic: the coff flavor carries the little-endian second linker member link.exe requires to resolve members at all. A closed VERB rather than an open name, because an archive layout is an ENGINE capability -- only variants `writeArArchive` realizes can be honored.
$targetArchComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: the .target.json NAME this format is for. `crossValidateTargetFormat` compares it against TargetSchema::name() -- two DECLARED NAMES -- where it used to run a six-arm `switch (format.kind())` reading a DIFFERENT field per identity (elf.machine / pe.machine / macho.cputype) and compare each against a hardcoded C++ table, kTargetArchMachineCodes, keyed on (target name x format kind). THAT TABLE IS DELETED, and the argument is ONE OWNER rather than tidiness: `arm64 is EM_AARCH64 = 183` had two owners -- this document's own machine field and that C++ row -- with nothing forcing them to agree, which is the identical shape as kCManglingRules and kAbiCatalog. The number now lives only in the document that emits it, and the pairing question is answered by a name this document states outright. Adding a new arch is now JSON-ONLY.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): THIS FORMAT DELIBERATELY DECLARES NO `predefinedMacros`, and the absence is an ANSWER rather than an omission -- it is the whole reason the channel lives on the FORMAT and not on the target. `dataModel` above is LLP64, so `__LP64__`/`_LP64` must NOT be defined here: MEASURED 2026-07-30, `/usr/bin/clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` (Apple clang 21.0.0) defines NEITHER, while the SAME clang defines BOTH on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and x86_64-apple-darwin -- the same CPU, differing only by object format, which is precisely why a target-side row would be a lie on this leg. Adding either spelling here would make the Windows headers take their LP64 arms against a 32-bit `long`. Pinned in the NEGATIVE direction by tests/link/test_object_format_schema.cpp.
$bitFieldStrategyComment: D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-ABI-EXACT: MSVC x64 bit-field packing, same as the PE siblings.
$unnamedBitFieldAlignmentComment: D-CSUBSET-ZERO-WIDTH-BITFIELD-ALIGNMENT: an UNNAMED bit-field contributes NO alignment. MEASURED with cl.exe 19.51 (`_Static_assert` on sizeof AND __alignof): `struct { char c; unsigned :0; char d; }` is 2/1. ~ DECLARED FOR COMPLETENESS AND DELIBERATELY NOT LOAD-BEARING: `msvc_straddle` never reads this key, because the MSVC rule is a property OF that strategy -- a zero-width field is INERT unless it terminates an open allocation unit, and when it does it folds its type's alignment and bumps the high-water. That is measured identical on x64 and arm64 PE, so there is nothing per-format left to declare. The key is stated so this document answers the same question every other C-ABI format answers, rather than being silently exempt for a reason a reader would have to reconstruct.
$externCallDispatchComment: Same call-site shape as the exec image: one `jmp *[IAT slot]` code thunk per extern FUNCTION and a plain `call rel32 -> thunk` at the site -- pc-relative, so the code needs no fixup when the loader rebases the DLL. D-FFI-EXTERN-CALL-DISPATCH + D-FFI-PE-IMPORT-THUNK.
$dataImportBindingComment: c149 (D-LK-EXTERN-DATA-IMPORT, the PE half): extern library DATA objects bind via the IAT slot itself (`__imp_<name>` semantics -- the loader import-resolves every IAT slot to the exported symbol's address, function or data alike) and the shared GotIndirect lowering reads it. Identical on exec and dll: the import machinery is the loader's, not the artifact flavor's.
$runtimeLibrariesComment: UCRT-P4 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION): the ROLE -> IMAGE table, and the single owner of 'which image plays which runtime role' for this format. The general argument for a TABLE rather than one `crt` string is made at length in pe64-x86_64-windows-exec.format.json's $runtimeLibrariesComment and is deliberately NOT restated here -- duplicated prose rots independently of its original. What is SPECIFIC to the .dll is WHY THIS TABLE HAS EXACTLY ONE ROW while the exec sibling has three, because the two missing roles are DELIBERATE ABSENCES and not an unfinished copy. (a) `cLibrary` is absent because NOTHING on this format names it: a DSS DLL ships AddressOfEntryPoint = 0 with no DllMain (D-LK2-DLL-DLLMAIN-ENTRY), validate() rejects the whole entry cluster here exactly as the ELF dyn schema does, and so there is no `processExit` asking for `exit` and no `processArgs` asking for an argv accessor. A .dll does not terminate a process, so it cannot honestly name the image that would. (b) `systemPrimitives` is absent because its only consumer is `librarySynthesis`, which this file deliberately does not declare -- see the NO-`librarySynthesis` clause of $comment above, which argues that the win32 <threads.h> shim inside a DLL is an unwitnessed form and should fail loud rather than ship. * NEITHER ABSENCE IS A STYLE CHOICE THE AUTHOR COULD HAVE GONE THE OTHER WAY ON, and that is the point of the table's bidirectional rule: the loader REFUSES a row that no block names, as inert config ('declares runtime-library role ... that NO block in this format names'), so pasting either row in would make this format fail AT LOAD and redden every test that loads it. A table can therefore never assert more than the format's blocks actually claim, which is precisely what makes the mechanical exit criterion (no pe table names msvcrt.dll, across all four pe flavours) worth checking rather than a value with no consumer. * WHY THE ROW EXISTS AT ALL, MEASURED 2026-08-10: before this block, a `__try` in a translation unit compiled for x86_64:pe64-x86_64-windows-dll was REFUSED -- `synthesizeSehFunclets: 1 SEH region(s) resolved but object format 'pe64-x86_64-windows-dll' declares NO sehPersonality block` -- which is a wrong-reject a USER finds rather than one we find, since real Windows DLLs use __try constantly.
$sehPersonalityComment: UCRT-P4 (D-WIN64-SEH-FUNCLETS + D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION): the routine an emitted UNWIND_INFO names as its EHANDLER, plus the ROLE that owns the image it is imported from. Declared here and not only on the exec sibling because A DLL CAN CONTAIN `__try`, which is not a hypothetical -- much of Windows itself is written that way -- and a format declaring no personality REFUSES such a translation unit outright. MEASURED 2026-08-10, both arms: WITHOUT this block, `__try` compiled for x86_64:pe64-x86_64-windows-dll failed rc=1 at `synthesizeSehFunclets`; WITH it, rc=0 and the emitted .dll carries BOTH `.xdata` (the UNWIND_INFO with UNW_FLAG_EHANDLER and the __C_specific_handler scope table) AND `.pdata` (the RUNTIME_FUNCTION rows the OS unwinder binary-searches), so the handler is genuinely REACHABLE rather than merely accepted. The role is `unwindPersonality` rather than `cLibrary` even though ucrtbase.dll would serve both: sameness is a fact about this DLL configuration, not about the model (Microsoft names the C library and the VC runtime separately in both /MD and /MT), and here the distinction is load-bearing rather than theoretical, because this format declares NO cLibrary row at all. MEASURED that the image choice is link-safe: `__C_specific_handler` is exported by ucrtbase (ord 30), msvcrt (106), ntdll (2332) and vcruntime140 (8). * READ THIS BEFORE COPYING THE BLOCK INTO THE .obj OR .lib SIBLING, because the `synthesizeSehFunclets` diagnostic's own advice ('Add the block') is WRONG for those two: `pe::encode`'s Obj arm attaches no FrameUnwindInfo and emits no `.pdata`/`.xdata` whatsoever (AssembledFunction::unwind is nullopt on the object path by construction, and SehScopeEntry is consumed only by the image-side .xdata emitter). MEASURED 2026-08-10 by actually declaring this block on both of them: the compile then SUCCEEDS rc=0 and the emitted seh.obj / seh.lib carry `.text` ONLY -- the filter funclets and the scope table are SILENTLY DROPPED, and the `__except` body can never run. That trades today's loud, correct refusal for a silent miscompile, which is the one outcome this project's bar rules out unconditionally; so those two files record the absence as deliberate, with the measurement, instead. This block is legal HERE because `pe.type = dll` routes through the SAME `encodeExec` substrate the .exe image uses (see $comment above), and that substrate is what emits the two unwind sections.
$supportedDataSectionsComment: rodata (read-only `.rdata`), data (mutable `.data`), bss (zero-init), relro (reloc-bearing CONST data, c145 -- folded into `.rdata`; the loader applies the IMAGE_REL_BASED_DIR64 base relocations into the slots at map time, before the page is exposed read-only, exactly as on the exec image; in a RELOCATABLE-AT-LOAD .dll that fold is LOAD-BEARING, not a hardening nicety). NO tdata/tbss: static TLS in a DLL needs the LoadLibrary static-TLS loader arc (IMAGE_TLS_DIRECTORY processing for late-loaded modules + DLL_THREAD_ATTACH-less threads -- D-LK-DLL-TLS-MODEL, not implemented); the linker's pre-walker gate rejects every thread_local loudly by this set's absence, mirroring the ELF dyn schema's D-LK-DYN-TLS-MODEL stance.
$artifactProfilesComment: This format SERVES the shared-library profile (plan 06 AP3), mirroring elf64-x86_64-linux-dyn. The cli profile is NOT served (a .dll is not a runnable console binary). ★ `module` JOINED THIS SET 2026-08-15 (plan 06 §5.1 B.12, as CORRECTED): a module IS a library, so it is served by every format that serves `lib` or `staticlib` and by nothing else. `artifactProfile` says what a project builds ITSELF as; `DependencyComposition` says how it is CONSUMED (`module` is SourceMerge — a consumer takes its SOURCES and ignores its artifact). Those are orthogonal, so a module builds standalone like any other library and the static-vs-dynamic choice is made by the `<target>:<format>` spec the author writes in `targets[]`, exactly as it already is for `lib` vs `staticlib` — no new rule and no engine change.

pe.$comment: IMAGE_FILE_HEADER identity. machine = IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_AMD64 (0x8664). characteristics = IMAGE_FILE_EXECUTABLE_IMAGE (0x0002) | IMAGE_FILE_LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE (0x0020) | IMAGE_FILE_DLL (0x2000) = 0x2022 -- byte-identical to `cl /LD` ground truth (dumpbin: 'Executable / Application can handle large addresses / DLL'). EXECUTABLE_IMAGE is required on DLLs too (PE COFF: absent means 'linker error'; the loader refuses the file); IMAGE_FILE_DLL is what makes CreateProcess reject it and LoadLibrary accept it. type = dll routes the walker's Dll arm.

optionalHeader.$comment: IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER64 (PE/COFF spec 3.4). magic = PE32+ (0x20B). imageBase = 0x180000000 (the MSVC x64 DLL preferred base; the loader rebases via the `.reloc` DIR64 table when ASLR or a base collision moves the image -- unlike the ELF .so there is NO base-0 layout trick: PE VAs are absolute at the preferred base and the loader adjusts each DIR64 site by the load delta). sectionAlignment = 0x1000, fileAlignment = 0x200 (MSVC defaults, same as the exec). subsystem = IMAGE_SUBSYSTEM_WINDOWS_GUI (2) -- the `cl /LD` convention; ignored by the loader for a library mapped into an existing process. dllCharacteristics = HIGH_ENTROPY_VA (0x0020) | DYNAMIC_BASE (0x0040) | NX_COMPAT (0x0100) = 0x160 -- dumpbin ground truth for a `cl /LD` DLL (no TERMINAL_SERVER_AWARE: link.exe sets 0x8000 on executables only; it is a per-process flag). DYNAMIC_BASE is deliberately KEPT so every load exercises the base-relocation machinery. Stack/heap reserve+commit are loader-ignored for DLLs (the process' exe owns them) but link.exe stamps them anyway -- same values as the exec sibling.

$staticInitializersComment: D-C-GNU-CONSTRUCTOR-ATTRIBUTE-IS-WARNED-AND-IGNORED-NOT-RUN: THIS FORMAT DECLARES NO STATIC-INITIALIZER CHANNEL, AND THE ABSENCE IS THE ANSWER RATHER THAN AN OMISSION -- recorded here so nobody 'completes' the table by adding one.\nThis is an IMAGE flavor that is NOT an EXEC flavor: `isExecFlavor()` is false, so DSS injects no entry trampoline and there is no DSS-synthesized entry to call anything. Nor will the platform: ld.so runs `DT_INIT_ARRAY`, a DYNAMIC TAG the ELF writer does not emit (MEASURED on a DSS image -- `readelf -d` lists eleven tags and none is an init tag), and a PE DLL's initializers run from `DllMain`/`_DllMainCRTStartup`, which DSS does not synthesize either.\nSo both runners would be FALSE here, and declaring the SECTIONS with no runner would emit a table nothing walks -- the silent shape this anchor exists to remove. With nothing declared, a program that schedules an initializer for this format is REFUSED by the linker, naming the format and the remedy. Making it work needs a real capability first (emit DT_INIT_ARRAY/DT_INIT_ARRAYSZ, or synthesize a DllMain), not a config row. Contrast macho64-*-dylib, which DOES declare `imageLoader`: dyld really does run `__mod_init_func` in a dylib, so that arm is a capability DSS has.

sections.$comment: Executable code section. virtualAddress = 0x1000 (RVA -- first page after the headers). Characteristics = IMAGE_SCN_CNT_CODE | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_EXECUTE | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ | IMAGE_SCN_ALIGN_16BYTES = 0x60500020, same as the exec sibling.
sections.name: .text

sections.$comment: Read-only data (string literals, reloc-free const globals; relro items fold in here with their DIR64 base-reloc sites). virtualAddress = 0 -- walker-computed (contiguous after .text). Characteristics = CNT_INITIALIZED_DATA | MEM_READ = 0x40000040.
sections.name: .rdata

sections.$comment: Writable initialized data. virtualAddress = 0 -- walker-computed. Characteristics = CNT_INITIALIZED_DATA | MEM_READ | MEM_WRITE = 0xC0000040.
sections.name: .data

sections.$comment: Zero-initialized data (SizeOfRawData = 0 -- no file bytes; the loader zero-fills). Characteristics = CNT_UNINITIALIZED_DATA | MEM_READ | MEM_WRITE = 0xC0000080.
sections.name: .bss

relocations.$comment: Same image-side kinds as the exec sibling, minus the tls SECREL row (this schema advertises no thread-local sections; a tls-kind relocation reaching the walker fails loud at the kind-declared check). REL32 is pc-relative -- needs no load-time fixup under rebase. abs64 data slots (fn-ptr tables, &global initializers, jump tables) are patched with their preferred-base VAs AND given IMAGE_REL_BASED_DIR64 `.reloc` rows the loader adjusts by the load delta.
relocations.name: IMAGE_REL_AMD64_REL32
